thread.title: Morning Movers: Tesla Keeps Cruising, but Can’t Keep the Dow From Falling - Barron's

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Morning Movers: Tesla Keeps Cruising, but Can’t Keep the Dow From Falling - Barron's
text:
By Teresa Rivas Aug. 2, 2018 9:19 a.m. ET The Hangover. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was falling in early trading , dinged by trade war worries. Not that that's hurting Tesla (TSLA), which was soaring after its second-quarter earnings report . Yet it doesn't have the pull of Apple (AAPL) to lift other stocks out of a tariff funk. We also have the Fed's language from Wednesday to parse. In today's Morning Movers , we...
•...review the Fed's move and trade worries;
•...preview Friday's jobs report ;
•...check in on Tesla (TSLA) post earnings.
A Whoosh & a Whimper
The trade war is back.
Illustration: Getty Images The Dow Jones Industrial Average futures are 156 points, or 0.6%, lower at 9:01 a.m., while S&P 500 futures are falling 0.5% and Nasdaq Composite futures are off 0.7%.
Trade worries are back at the forefront of investor minds this morning: Apple's (AAPL) earnings put a shine on the market yesterday, when the news first broke. But reality has set in today, as escalation from the U.S.—it's considering imposing tariffs of up to 25% on $200 billion of Chinese goods—boost tensions again.
Bluster and threats are nothing new in this war, but "one issue with everyone knowing tariffs and rhetoric are negotiating tactics is the fact that everyone realizes the will to leave them on is only as strong as the political strength the administration holds." writes First Franklin's Brett Ewing. "We worry that the window to yield strength from the Trump side is narrow and real agreements need to be getting struck soon."
Elsewhere, markets are still digesting the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates steady on Wednesday, as expected, even if more rate increases are likely before year's end: Lazard Asset Management's Ronald Temple calls September rate hike an apparent "slam dunk" at this point.
Yet even here the threat of tariffs looms. The central bank must "walk a tightrope" between economic overheating and rising inflation, while still keeping one eye on a potential trade war, writes Independent Advisor Alliance Chief Investment Officer Chris Zaccarelli. While the market now expects a third rate hike (and maybe another December, absent a trade war or other nasty surprise), the pace of increases is "evidence that the economy is very strong."
That said, he notes that the yield on 10-year T-notes is one to watch as it "could be the canary in the coal mine to divine whether the bond market feels the trade tensions will knock the economy off course." If it falls below 2.75%, we may be in for trouble.
When it comes to tariff worries, Treasury yields may be telling, but Osterweis Capital Management Chairman John Osterweis doesn't think that equity markets are truly pricing in either the best-case scenario (the White House's "bellicose trade rhetoric is simply a negotiating tactic" to get us to a fair-trade outcome) or a worst-case scenario (expanding tit-for-tat tariffs). As a trade war remains the biggest threat to the U.S. economy, Osterweis argues investors should be positioning themselves by owning stocks with company-specific fundamental outlooks that are less dependent on either trade outcome.
Illustration: Bloomberg News Foreign sales made up 30% of S&P 500 companies' revenues last year, up from 29% in 2016. While the majority—some 10 percentage points—come from Europe where we may be inching closer to an agreement, eight percentage points come from Asia, and 2% of total S&P revenues is tied directly to China, writes Goldman Sachs' David Kostin.
If trade tensions escalate, he advises favoring companies with high domestic revenues, while an easing in tensions may see companies with greater China exposure, such as semiconductors, outperform.
Trade war aside, now that the Fed has spoken, investors will likely be looking forward to tomorrow's jobs report on the economic data front. As is usual, the jobs number will likely set the tone for the markets in the following weeks, writes the Leuthold Group's Jim Paulsen , and since January, the employment figures have been "reassuring."
That said, the reports have presented a bit of a conundrum, as salaries haven't budged much despite a tight labor market. Paulsen wouldn't be surprised to see another "tame wage number" tomorrow, but warns that it can't stay that way forever, and employers will eventually have to pay up: "A wage whoosh is coming!"
We're going to need it to pay higher prices on all those imports.
Morning Movers
Earnings & News
Cigna (CI) is up 2.2% to $186.88 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The health insurer earned $3.89 a share on revenue of $11.5 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $3.30 on revenue of $11.2 billion. For the full year, it sees EPS of $13.60 to $1380, compared with the $13.21 consensus estimate. Activist investor Carl Icahn may also vote against its merger with Express Scripts (ESRX).
Clorox (CLX) is up 2.5% to $137.50 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The household products maker earned $1.66 a share on revenue of $1.69 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.59 on revenue of $1.72 billion. For the full year, it sees EPS of $6.32 to $6.52, on revenue of $6.24 billion to $6.37 billion. Consensus calls for earnings of $6.41 on revenue of $6.44 billion.
Concho Resources (CXO) is down 3.6% to $137.99 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The energy firm earned $1.24 a share on revenue of $945 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 94 cents on revenue of $906.82 million.
Express Scripts (ESRX) is up 1.3% to $75.40 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The pharmacy benefit manager earned $2.22 a share on revenue of $25.64 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $2.20 a share on revenue of $25.43 billion. For the full year, it sees EPS of $9 to $9.14, on revenue of $99 billion to $102 billion. Consensus calls for earnings of $9.05 on revenue of $100.99 billion.
Fitbit (FIT) is up 2.5% to $6.07 after reporting second-quarter earning s. The wearable fitness device firm lost 22 cents a share, on revenue of $299.34 million. Analysts were looking for a 24-cent loss on revenue of $285.4 million. For the full year, it sees revenues of $1.5 billion, compared with the $1.47 billion consensus estimate.
Herbalife (HLF) is up 1.8% to $52.01 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The nutrition and supplement firm earned 80 cents a share on revenue of $1.3 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 68 cents on revenue of $1.26 billion. For the full year, it sees EPS of $2.60 to $2.80, compared with the $2.73 consensus estimate.
Kellogg (K) is up 1.6% to $68.34 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The packaged food maker earned $1.14 a share on revenue of $3.36 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.05 on revenue of $3.31 billion.
Qorvo (QRVO) is down 3.9% to $79 after reporting first-quarter earnings. The chip maker earned 96 cents a share on revenue of $692.7 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 76 cents a share on revenue of $656.97 million.
Square (SQ) is down 2.2% to $65.38 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The fintech firm earned 13 cents a share on revenue of $385 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 11 cents on revenue of $367.99 million. For the full year, it sees EPS of 42 cents to 46 cents compared with the 46 cent consensus estimate.
Tesla (TSLA) is up 9.9% to $330.75 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The electric car maker lost $3.06 a share, missing analyst forecasts for a loss of $2.88 a share, on sales of $4 billion, which was just ahead of predictions for $3.99 billion.
Illustration: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images TripAdvisor (TRIP) is down 12.9% to $50.20 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The online travel agency and review site earned 41 cents a share on revenue of $433 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 40 cents on revenue of $434.86 million.
Wynn Resorts (WYNN) is down 4.5% to $152.80 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The casino operator earned $1.53 a share on revenue of $1.61 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.97 a share on revenue of $1.72 billion.
Yum Brands (YUM) is down 2.5% to $77.45 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The restaurant chain earned 82 cents a share on revenue of $1.37 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 74 cents on revenue of $1.36 billion.
Upgrades & Downgrades
Bunge (BG) is down 0.8% to $65.50 after JPMorgan downgraded it to Neutral.
Royal Dutch Shell (RDS.A) is down 1.9% to $66.22 after Morgan Stanley downgraded it to Equal Weight.
Yum China (YUMC) is down 1.9% to $34.97 after Macquarie downgraded it to Neutral.
